around.headline: Six arrested after violence during Eid Milad procession in Bengaluru
around.summary: Bengaluru police arrested six people, including one identified as Puneeth Kerehalli, and registered three FIRs over assault and sloganeering after clashes broke out during an Eid Milad procession, per today's reports. If you're near an affected neighbourhood this weekend, expect a heavier police presence and possible diversions around procession routes.
around.source: The News Minute, The Hindu, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Suspected illegal-arms supplier shot in leg after attacking Bengaluru cops with sword
around.summary: A suspected weapons supplier attacked police with a sword and chilli powder during a midnight raid; officers said they opened fire in self-defence and the man was shot in the leg, per today's report. Part of a wider crackdown that also saw police screen nearly 500 rowdy-sheeters across the city this week.

around.headline: Namma Metro Green Line hit by technical glitch today
around.summary: BMRCL confirmed a technical glitch disrupted Green Line services today, and separately the Purple Line's older trains go in for a six-week, speed-restricted mid-life overhaul starting soon, per today's reports. Budget extra travel time on both lines this week if they're on your route.

around.headline: 40 drunk-driving cases booked after Bengaluru police screen 1,476 water tanker drivers
around.summary: Traffic police booked 40 drunk-driving cases in a targeted screening drive of nearly 1,500 water tanker drivers, per today's report — tankers have been involved in several recent close calls with two-wheeler riders. Give tankers extra room on narrow roads, especially at night.

around.headline: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns from cabinet a second time over same corruption scandal
around.summary: B Nagendra quit the Karnataka cabinet again over the same corruption scandal he had resigned for once before, framing it today as a targeted political fight, per today's report. A story worth tracking if you follow state governance and welfare-scheme spending.

around.headline: Citizens and experts push back harder on Bengaluru parkland amendment
around.summary: Experts and residents are pressing for a full rollback — not just a cap — of the state amendment that would allow parkland to be repurposed for development, with fresh op-eds and statements out today, per today's reports. If you use a city park regularly, this decision could affect whether it stays protected green space.
around.source: The Hindu, The New Indian Express, The News Minute

around.headline: Nepal flash-flood death toll climbs to 547
around.summary: The death toll from Nepal's flash floods has risen to 547 with fears of fresh flooding, and Karnataka's chief minister's office says 13 state residents remain stranded and 4 NRI pilgrims are still missing, per today's reports. If you have relatives travelling in the region, stay in touch and watch for state helpline updates.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

street_smart.title: You're waiting at a Bengaluru bus stop scrolling your phone when a biker swoops past and snatches it clean out of your hand before speeding off into traffic. You're not hurt, but the phone — with your banking apps and UPI — is gone. What's the single most important thing to do in the next few minutes?
street_smart.based_on: No single incident in today's feeds fits the choice-based trap format cleanly (today's Bengaluru safety stories are a sword attack on police during a raid, arrests after an Eid Milad clash, and a jewellery-showroom theft — none lend themselves to a choice scenario), so this rotates in from the evergreen list: phone snatching response (CEIR blocking). This specific topic hasn't appeared as the street-smart scenario in the last three weeks of briefs (Aug 7–28), which instead covered digital-arrest scams, UPI QR fraud, auto/cab overcharging, two-wheeler theft, tenant/landlord rights, and various road-safety and civic incidents.
street_smart.situation: The bike is already out of sight, and you have maybe a few minutes before someone could swap the SIM or try to use your accounts.

choices.text: Call your telecom to block the SIM immediately, then go to ceir.gov.in (or dial 14422) to register the phone's IMEI so it's blocked across every network, and file a police e-FIR with that IMEI number.
choices.feedback: Correct. Blocking the SIM stops your number from being misused right away, but it's the CEIR (Central Equipment Identity Register) step that blacklists the phone's IMEI across every telecom operator in the country — so even if the thief swaps in a new SIM, the handset itself becomes unusable. A police report alone can't do that.

choices.text: Don't bother reporting right away — since expensive phones rarely get recovered, wait a few days to see if it turns up before going through the hassle of blocking it.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Every hour the SIM and IMEI stay unblocked is a window for someone to reset OTPs, drain UPI-linked accounts, or resell a fully working phone. Recovery odds don't matter here — blocking the device fast is what actually protects your money and identity, independent of whether you ever get the phone back.

choices.text: Call your bank first to freeze UPI and net-banking access, but put off blocking the SIM and IMEI for later since the phone is probably gone for good.
choices.feedback: Freezing your accounts is a reasonable instinct, but delaying the SIM block leaves your number live for OTP interception, and skipping CEIR means the phone stays usable and resellable — both matter even if you never see it again.

choices.text: File a police complaint straightaway, but skip the CEIR (ceir.gov.in) step since the report alone should be enough to stop the phone from being used.
choices.feedback: Filing a report is necessary but not sufficient — police reports document the theft, they don't technically stop the phone from working. Only a CEIR IMEI block actually renders the device useless on any network.

takeaways: ceir.gov.in or 14422 blocks a stolen phone's IMEI across every telecom operator in India, turning it into a brick even if the thief swaps the SIM — a police report alone can't do this.
Block your SIM with your telecom within minutes of the theft; every minute it stays active is a window for OTP interception or UPI misuse.
Dial *#06# on your phone right now (or check the box/bill) to find your IMEI, and save it somewhere separate from the phone — you'll need it fast if this happens.

quiz.question: Which Indian state shares the longest border with Nepal, the country hit by this week's deadly flash floods?
quiz.why: Bihar's border with Nepal runs over 700 km, longer than any other Indian state's, which is why floods and landslides there often affect Bihar first.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age set by the Indian Constitution to contest an election to the Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: 18 is the minimum age to vote, but a candidate must be at least 25 to contest a Lok Sabha or state assembly seat.
